item.title: Hegseth honors guard who scolded his group at the Tomb of Unknown Soldier
item.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday honored the Army sentinel who forcefully scolded members of his entourage for laughing and talking near Arlington National Cemetery's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day.  

Hegseth posted a photo of himself on social media pinning a Joint Service Commendation Medal on the unidentified soldier’s chest.

“We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist,” Hegseth wrote. “Carry on Patriots.” 

On Veterans Day, Hegseth, his wife Jennifer, and three of his top deputies were seen posing for photographs on the steps overlooking the tomb, which has provided a final resting place for several of America’s unidentified service members — and a site of reflection and mourning — since 1921. Members of the group could be heard chuckling and chatting as they ascended the steps. 

We love soldiers.
We love standards.
Well done, Specialist.

Carry on Patriots. pic.twitter.com/Uk6ek6oOso

— Secretary of War Pete Hegseth (@SecWar) November 12, 2026

The sentinel — a member of the Army’s 3rd Infantry Regiment, known as The Old Guard — stepped forward and shouted in their direction: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!” 

Video of the encounter, which followed the annual Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, spread quickly online. 

A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery. As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be… pic.twitter.com/dIPp8wMGEG

— The Associated Press (@AP) November 11, 2026

On Wednesday evening, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell issued a statement saying the soldier had acted appropriately. 

“While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum,” Parnell said.

Joint Service Commendation Medals are awarded to members of the Armed Forces who distinguish themselves while serving in a joint activity or on joint military staff.

Hegseth’s Veterans Day flap follows his brush with impeachment earlier this week. On Tuesday, the Republican-controlled U.S. House of Representatives voted to effectively kill the articles of impeachment against Hegseth — for now — by blocking their consideration on the House floor and sending them back to the Judiciary Committee, where GOP leaders can hold them up until the next Congress is seated in January 2027.

Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, reintroduced impeachment charges against Hegseth on Monday, alleging that the embattled Pentagon chief had committed "high crimes and misdemeanors" and abused the power of his office by violating the War Powers Resolution, conducting military operations without congressional authorization and ordering unlawful military actions in several countries.

Democrats — who voted unanimously against shelving the impeachment charges — will have a large House majority next year after winning at least 255 seats in last week's midterm elections. They have already vowed to try to remove Hegseth from office when they take control of Congress, building on voter dissatisfaction with the war in Iran. 

"In the majority, one of the first things we're gonna do is run Pete Hegseth out of town," Democratic Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, the minority leader who is poised to become House speaker, said at a rally last month.

Hegseth would be just the third Cabinet official in U.S. history to be impeached, and the second in three years.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/hegseth-honors-guard-who-scolded-him-at-tomb-of-the-unknown-soldier-171707681.html

item.title: A wintry forecast of snow expected to give way to warmer-than-average temperatures
item.description:
Snow is likely to fall in the mountains of New York and northern New England Thursday night as a storm system — aka a developing nor'easter — currently dumping rain across the Mid-Atlantic moves north and encounters colder air from the north.

The National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center (WPC) said in its latest forecast that as the colder air wraps around the storm, rain will turn to snow overnight into Friday at higher elevations in New York, northeastern Pennsylvania and northern New England — likely making the roads hazardous.

Those at lower elevations will mostly see rain through Thursday night, with a wintry mix possible Friday morning. Wet snow is also possible in the southern and central Appalachians, mainly from Friday night into Saturday morning — some areas could see their first snowflakes of the season.

In Michigan's Upper Peninsula, heavy lake-effect snow will bring "significant accumulation" through Friday, the WPC said.

The nor'easter is expected to strengthen as it moves into the Northeast through Thursday evening, after bringing scattered thunderstorms and gusty winds to the Ohio and Tennessee valleys earlier in the day. Its center is expected to pass east of Cape Cod.

Steady rain is expected to spread over southern New England Thursday evening, possibly becoming heavy at times near the coast, according to the WPC, which also forecasts increasing northeasterly winds and minor coastal flooding around high tide near New York City.

Following the storm, polar air will then spread across much of the central and eastern U.S., with temperatures well below normal by Friday. Freezing temperatures are forecast to reach the Deep South by Saturday morning, setting up a widespread frost and freeze across the South and Southeast this weekend.

Is snow likely?

Mostly in the mountains. The WPC said rain will turn to snow Thursday night and into Friday at higher elevations in New York, northeastern Pennsylvania and northern New England, where accumulating snow is likely.

AccuWeather said Pittsburgh, Syracuse and Binghamton could see their first snowflakes of the season, along with the Poconos, Catskills and Berkshires. Wet snow is also possible in the southern and central Appalachians from Friday night into Saturday morning, the WPC said.

But AccuWeather senior meteorologist Adam Douty said, "outside of higher elevations, snow should struggle to accumulate."

As it stands, most coastal areas and lower-lying parts of the Northeast, including Philadelphia, New York and Boston, are more likely to see rain than snow.

Is the nor'easter linked to the polar vortex?

The early weakening of the polar vortex, which started last week, has left many wondering whether a blast of icy weather is on its way as a result. But forecasters have said it's not that clear. 

While the WPC's latest forecast refers to polar air, meaning a mass of very cold air from Canada, it doesn't mention the polar vortex.

Tyler Roys, a meteorologist at AccuWeather, told Yahoo it is "hard to say if there is any connection between the two." He said most of the impacts from an early polar vortex disruption are "going towards eastern Europe and Asia."

If the vortex has any influence, Roys said, it is likely tied to the cold arriving behind the storm, though "the influence of the polar vortex appears to be limited."

Roys added that forecasters "do feel that there could be an increase of influence from the polar vortex towards the end of November into December" as the current pattern fades and a new one sets up.

Laura Ciasto, a meteorologist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), told Yahoo that the vortex has been "displaced for well over a week," though it hasn't yet reached the threshold for a sudden stratospheric warming, a rapid warming high in the atmosphere that can weaken or split the vortex.

"It's possible we are seeing that effect at the surface now," she said. "It's a classic chicken-or-the-egg situation."

What is a nor'easter?

A nor'easter is a storm situated along the East Coast of the U.S., with its namesake reflecting that the winds over the coastal area are usually from the northeast, the NWS says. 

It forms when an area of lower air pressure draws in surrounding air and strengthens near the coast. It is often fueled by the clash of cold air from the north and warm, moist air over the Gulf Stream.

While these storms can happen at any time of year, they are usually at their strongest between the colder months, from September through April.

Nor'easters "nearly always" bring precipitation in the form of heavy rain or snow, the NWS says, as well as winds of gale force, rough seas and, sometimes, coastal flooding. 

The most violent nor'easters have caused billions of dollars in damage. The storm is expected to be less severe than September's early-season nor'easter, which killed a New York City Housing Authority worker, flooded coastal communities and left more than 130,000 customers without power across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, the Associated Press reported.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/weather-news/article/a-noreaster-is-soaking-the-coast-who-could-see-the-first-snow-of-the-season-173445911.html

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns as new affair allegations emerge
item.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock tanked Thursday after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The company's CFO, Colette Kress, will serve as the interim head of the business until a permanent successor is named.

Nvidia stock dropped 13% on the news before paring losses.

The leadership shakeup followed a report from The New York Times on Wednesday that embattled Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair. The company's board was reportedly meeting on Wednesday night to determine if it will oust Huang as chief executive, the Wall Street Journal reports.

According to the report, Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell.

Follow along for live updates and reactions.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo Finance at https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/live/nvidia-live-updates-jensen-huang-ousted-cfo-colette-kress-to-serve-as-interim-ceo-165956717.html

item.title: 1 dead, 4 wounded in a shooting in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle
item.description:
At least five people were wounded and one was killed during a shooting in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle neighborhood early Thursday, police said.

The gunman, who then barricaded himself inside an apartment building, later died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Officers responded to reports of an active shooting at a gym just before 8 a.m. ET, Metropolitan Police Department interim chief Jeffery Carroll said at a press briefing.

Once inside, police located one victim, who died at the scene, Carroll said. Four others were wounded and transported to local hospitals. One of the victims was in critical condition, he said. Three had non-life-threatening injuries.

As officers were clearing the gym and an adjacent building, shots rang out from the seventh floor, where the suspect barricaded himself inside an apartment, Carroll said.

Much of the block was cordoned off, and nearby schools were placed on temporary lockdown.

While police were attempting to negotiate with the barricaded suspect, he fatally shot himself, Carroll said.

Police did not immediately identify the gunman. Carroll said that investigators believe the suspect had “some sort of conflict” with the apartment building’s homeowners association.

While the suspect was barricaded, a fire broke out in the building, Carroll said. The building’s sprinkler system was activated, and the fire has since been extinguished, he said.

James Spellman, who was at the gym, told the Associated Press that there were about 50 people there when the shooting began.

"Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out," Spellman said. "One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck."

Witness Ryan Dubicki said he was in his apartment around 8 a.m. when he "heard about five bangs."

"They were really spread out so I thought it was construction," Dubicki told AP. His building's managers sent a notice about a possible active shooter.

Another witness, Max Smith, told reporters that he heard gunshots and took shelter in a nearby shop. "I'm very shaken up," Smith said. "You know, you don't expect it."

The shootings, which occurred just a mile from the White House, prompted a massive law enforcement response. Federal agencies, including the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, said they sent agents to the scene to help.

This is a breaking news story. Refresh this page for updates.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/1-dead-4-wounded-in-shooting-in-washington-dcs-logan-circle-shooter-barricaded-himself-in-building-police-say-154319642.html

item.title: At least 8 dead, including 2 children, after building collapses in Brooklyn, officials say
item.description:
At a press conference on Thursday afternoon, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani provided updates on the Brooklyn building collapse, saying that six adults and two children were among the eight people who died on Wednesday. Two of the adults who died were construction workers.

“This has been a devastating evening and morning for our city,” Mamdani said.

Mamdani also confirmed that 18 other people were injured, including 14 civilians and four firefighters. The vast majority of those injured and being treated at hospitals are in stable condition, with one person in critical condition.

“I want to take a moment to remember those we have so senselessly lost. These were our friends and our neighbors, parents and children,” the mayor said. “Young families building their lives in our city and immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, Trinidad and beyond. Let us continue to hold close those who have been plunged into unimaginable grief and pray for a full and rapid recovery for every New Yorker injured.”

Mamdani also thanked the first responders and construction workers who helped dig through the rubble to find survivors. “People are alive today because of their heroism yesterday,” he said.

“Firefighters arrived on the scene in less than one minute after the 911 call first came in,” Mamdani added.

The American Red Cross has opened a reception center at the Flatbush YMCA for residents who were affected and displaced by the building collapse. Mamdani said the city and American Red Cross will continue to provide “expanded services” from the Flatbush YMCA for residents displaced by the building collapse, including temporary housing, assistance with social services and mental health support.

“Conditions will grow more challenging today with the rain, but operations will continue,” the mayor said. “A tragedy of this magnitude demands a comprehensive and thorough investigation that includes both the construction site and the building which collapsed.

Mamdani said that the investigation has already begun, with law enforcement leading it. “There are five main entities involved with this construction site, or associated, with approximately 100 other sites across the city. Our Department of Buildings is commencing sweeps of those sites today.”

This is a developing story. Check back for updates. Read the original story below.

At least eight people died and 18 others were injured, when a three-story building collapsed Wednesday in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York.

The four-unit apartment building crumpled into a construction site next to it at about 4 p.m. ET.

Those who were injured were taken to a hospital and included four in critical condition, officials said. Seven were children and three were firefighters. Authorities did not confirm if any children were among those killed.

In a post on X Thursday morning, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, "Rescue workers have spent the night searching the site of yesterday's building collapse, working under extremely dangerous conditions to find and save anyone who may still be trapped.

"I am heartbroken that eight New Yorkers have now lost their lives and at least 17 have been injured, including three firefighters. There are no words for a loss of this magnitude. My heart is with the families and loved ones of those we have lost, those who are injured and everyone grieving today."

Two deaths were announced on Wednesday, with six further deaths confirmed Thursday.

Water service was restored to about 100 buildings in the area on Thursday after the New York City Department of Environmental Protection had to shut down city water mains so that emergency crews could continue search and rescue operations, according to a post on X.

Rescuers searched for survivors into the night with about 250 first responders working at the scene. "We'll continue to look until we find everybody," FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said. A spokesperson for the FDNY told the New York Times Thursday that rescuers were still hoping to find survivors.

A pregnant woman was among those pulled out of the rubble. Footage broadcast by CBS News New York showed her being taken away on a stretcher more than two hours after the building collapsed, while her husband waited in anguish.

"She is alive. She is still alive. I'm very happy. I'm very happy. I'm very happy. I thank all of you guys," he told CBS News New York after she was rescued. "She's pregnant, six months."

Earlier, the man had been seen frantically looking for her. "I've heard nothing. She's inside the building. She's pregnant," he told reporters.

One resident, Anderson Velez, told the New York Post he was at work in the Bronx when his wife called him and said their children, ages 7 and 2, were trapped.

"She called me when the building collapsed while she was inside with rubble on top of her. She was screaming for someone to help get my son out and then the call cut off," he said, confirming his family was now safe.

An eyewitness, Melissa Orna, told the New York Times: "The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell."

The 1930s building fell into an adjoining construction site, where excavation work was ongoing. The cause of the collapse is under investigation, said John Esposito, the city's fire department chief. He said rescue teams may need to take several days to search the site for all potential victims.

Officials have described the search and rescue mission as "very dangerous," with firefighters and police officers punching holes through rubble in the search of survivors.

"Multiple people from the building and the construction site were trapped," Bonsignore said. "This will be a prolonged operation. Collapse operations are extremely dangerous. Every move is choreographed and critically important to patient outcomes and member safety. Members have been working methodically and haven't stopped since they arrived."

No official cause for the collapse has been released.

In April, the New York City Department of Buildings issued a violation to a demolition contractor at the construction site who "unlawfully continued work while on notice of a Stop Work Order," according to the violation. Inspectors noted that a single-story building was demolished despite the city's order to stop work. The violation was resolved in October, according to DOB records.

Yahoo has requested comment from the DOB about why the city ordered a work stoppage in the first place.

On Wednesday, DOB issued a full stop work order "due to unsafe construction operations causing adjacent building (1321 Flatbush Avenue) to collapse."

Mamdani said at a news conference Wednesday that rescue workers arrived on the scene within one minute of receiving the 911 call. He also confirmed some of the fatalities and said that injured people had been transported to local hospitals.

"This has been an incredibly challenging and fast-moving situation — with precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface," he said, adding, "This type of rescue is exactly what the FDNY trains for."

He also asked New Yorkers to "please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss."

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/brooklyn-building-collapse-at-least-5-dead-and-17-injured-as-rescuers-search-for-survivors-pregnant-woman-pulled-from-rubble-113416871.html
